facts.f: India is the world's largest democracy.
facts.e: Hundreds of millions of people vote in its general elections.

facts.f: India's Constitution is the longest written constitution of any country.
facts.e: It has a Preamble, hundreds of articles and many schedules.

facts.f: The Preamble of India's Constitution begins with 'We, the people of India'.
facts.e: It shows that the power of the government comes from the people.

facts.f: The Preamble calls India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
facts.e: It also promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all citizens.

facts.f: The Constitution gives six Fundamental Rights.
facts.e: Equality, freedom, protection from exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to go to court to protect these rights.

facts.f: The Right to Education gives free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14.
facts.e: It is part of Article 21A of the Constitution.

facts.f: Dr Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.
facts.e: It lets citizens go straight to the Supreme Court if their Fundamental Rights are taken away.

facts.f: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution in 1976.
facts.e: They include respecting the flag and anthem, protecting the environment and developing a scientific temper.

facts.f: India's Parliament has two houses: the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
facts.e: The President is also part of Parliament.

facts.f: In India, citizens can vote from the age of 18.
facts.e: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 in 1989.

facts.f: Lok Sabha elections are usually held every five years.
facts.e: The party or group with a majority in the Lok Sabha forms the government.

facts.f: The President is India's head of state. The Prime Minister is the head of government.
facts.e: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers run the government day to day.

facts.f: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house. It is never dissolved.
facts.e: One-third of its members retire every two years.

facts.f: The Supreme Court in New Delhi is India's highest court.
facts.e: Its decisions must be followed by all other courts.

facts.f: The Election Commission of India conducts elections.
facts.e: It was set up on 25 January 1950. That day is now National Voters' Day.

facts.f: India uses Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) in its elections.
facts.e: Voters press a button next to their candidate's name and symbol.

facts.f: Panchayati Raj is the system of village self-government in India.
facts.e: The Gram Panchayat looks after local matters like water, roads and cleanliness.

facts.f: The 73rd Amendment in 1992 gave panchayats a place in the Constitution.
facts.e: It came into force on 24 April 1993, now celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day.

facts.f: India has three levels of government: Union, State and Local.
facts.e: Each level looks after different matters.

facts.f: Government has three organs: the legislature, the executive and the judiciary.
facts.e: The legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out, and the judiciary interprets them and settles disputes.

facts.f: Writing India's Constitution took nearly three years.
facts.e: It took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

facts.f: The original Constitution was handwritten by calligrapher Prem Behari Narain Raizada.
facts.e: Its pages were decorated by artists from Santiniketan, led by Nandalal Bose.

facts.f: The original handwritten copies of the Constitution are kept in helium-filled cases.
facts.e: They are in the Library of Parliament, protected from damage.

facts.f: The ink put on a voter's finger is hard to wash off for days.
facts.e: It shows that the person has already voted, so nobody can vote twice.

facts.f: The Right to Information Act of 2005 lets citizens ask the government for information.
facts.e: It helps make the government more open and answerable.

facts.f: The United Nations was founded on 24 October 1945. Its headquarters are in New York.
facts.e: It works for peace, human rights and development.

facts.f: The UN Security Council has five permanent members.
facts.e: They are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.

facts.f: The Vice-President of India is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
facts.e: The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha.

facts.f: A bill becomes a law after both houses of Parliament pass it and the President signs it.
facts.e: The President's approval is called 'assent'.

facts.f: Abraham Lincoln described democracy as 'government of the people, by the people, for the people'.
facts.e: He said this in his Gettysburg Address in 1863.

facts.f: Voting in India is by secret ballot.
facts.e: No one can find out whom you voted for.

facts.f: Since 2013, Indian voters can choose NOTA: 'None of the Above'.
facts.e: It lets a voter reject all the candidates.

facts.f: Universal adult franchise means every adult citizen can vote.
facts.e: Religion, caste, gender, wealth or education do not matter.

facts.f: Article 17 of the Constitution abolished untouchability.
facts.e: Practising untouchability is a punishable offence.

facts.f: India's Constitution borrowed good ideas from other countries.
facts.e: For example, the parliamentary system came from Britain and the idea of Fundamental Rights from the USA.

facts.f: The Gram Sabha is made up of all the adult voters of a village.
facts.e: It meets to discuss the village's work and check the panchayat.

facts.f: Big cities are run by Municipal Corporations, headed by a Mayor.
facts.e: They look after things like water supply, garbage collection and street lights.

facts.f: The Directive Principles of State Policy guide the government in making laws.
facts.e: Unlike Fundamental Rights, they cannot be enforced in a court.

facts.f: 112 is India's single emergency helpline number.
facts.e: It connects you to police, fire and ambulance help.

facts.f: 1098 is a free helpline for children in India who need help.
facts.e: Any child, or an adult on a child's behalf, can call at any time.

facts.f: Rules at home and at school are a bit like laws.
facts.e: They help everyone live, learn and play together fairly and safely.
